source.title: Explore the Limits of Omni-modal Pretraining at Scale
source.authors: Yiyuan Zhang; Handong Li; Jing Liu; Xiang-Yu Yue

record.file_problem: No apparent truncation or document mismatch. The text is a full paper, though some figures are represented only by extracted labels and axes.
record.tranche_reason: The study sweeps multimodal model and data scales and reports downstream retrieval scores, bearing on V6. It does not use held-out language-model cross-entropy or fit the power laws in V1–V3.
record.gate_note: Table 7 reports separate retrieval scores across model sizes and data sizes; those scale-dependent downstream results are recorded below. The paper also shows training-loss curves in Figure 6, but does not report held-out loss values, numerical curve results, or power-law fits, so these do not test the specified loss-law versions. Benchmark scores in Tables 2–6 without a scale comparison are not scale-dependent results for these versions.
record.test_reason: Table 7 tests the scale-improvement component of V6 in omni-modal pretraining: three backbone sizes and four dataset sizes are compared on eight downstream retrieval tasks. It does not establish a quantitative prediction law, extrapolation accuracy, or a power-law loss relation.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's scaling paraphrase is substantially accurate: the authors report better downstream performance from larger MiCo backbones and potential for further data scaling. They call their ablations and training-loss plots multimodal scaling laws, but provide no fitted power-law exponents, predictive extrapolation test, or compute-optimal allocation. Their broader conclusion advocates MiCo's brain-inspired omni-modal architecture.
record.recipe_differences: This is a multimodal pretraining and downstream-benchmark scaling ablation, not the language-model held-out-loss measurement or compute-optimal fitting procedure in the cited scaling-law studies.
record.method_sensitivity: Reported downstream scores vary with model size and data scale; two data-scale task scores dip at 110M relative to 10M.

fits_no_version.finding: Figure 6 compares training-loss trajectories under modality, dataset, backbone, and objective changes, without readable numerical curve outcomes or a tested power-law form.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: MiCo training dynamics vary with its pretraining configuration.

fits_no_version.finding: Table 1 compares architecture variants on downstream retrieval and captioning, without fixed parameter counts or loss measurements.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Separating language and knowledge modalities into two branches improves MiCo downstream performance under the tested architecture choices.

record.problems: The scale ablations report downstream task metrics rather than held-out pretraining cross-entropy; no scaling exponents, prediction tests, or uncertainty estimates are provided. The paper says most hyperparameters are not precisely tuned.
record.rows_left_out: Table 7's reported Average column for the three model-scale conditions and four data-scale conditions is omitted to keep the record within 60 rows; the task-specific scores are retained. Figure 6 training-loss curves are not entered as rows because the text does not provide readable numerical outcomes or explicit curve descriptions and they are not held-out loss results.

untested.parts: Held-out language-model pretraining loss and power-law dependence on parameters, tokens, or compute over orders of magnitude.
Small-run fits predicting losses of substantially larger runs.
Loss-minimising parameter/token allocation at fixed compute and stable allocation exponents.
Loss comparisons across architectures at fixed parameter count; Table 1 reports downstream scores without matched parameter counts.
Power-law form in multimodal pretraining. Figure 6 contains training trajectories, not an evaluated power-law relation across scales.
Quantitative predictive accuracy, extrapolation to unseen scales, and prediction from pretraining loss; downstream tasks beyond retrieval are not compared across scales.
Sensitivity of fitted exponents or compute-optimal splits to setup and fitting choices, and departures from fitted power laws.

record.verdict_notes: All judgments use the supplied text. Table 7 supports descriptive scale trends, not quantitative predictability. Training steps are fixed at 30k in the ablation, which does not imply fixed compute across backbone sizes. Nominal data sizes conflict with Algorithm 2: 110M and 334M are implemented there as 11M and 33.4M; Figure 6 instead labels 100M and 300M. These inconsistencies constrain quantitative interpretation but do not establish V7. Omitted averages and Figure 6 were already declared in rows_left_out.

versions.untested_parts: Held-out language-model pretraining loss versus parameters, tokens, or compute; power-law behavior and orders of magnitude.
Fitting on small runs and predicting much larger runs.
Fixed-compute optimization and parameter/token allocation trends.
Loss differences across depth, width, or architecture at fixed parameter count.
Whether a power-law form holds in other modalities or training regimes; no power-law fit or held-out loss test is reported.
The study reports downstream retrieval scores across model and data scales, but does not test predictability from pretraining loss or fit a quantitative predictive law.
Dependence of fitted exponents or compute-optimal allocations on setup and fitting choices.

relationships.condition: Model-scale ablation, Base-86M→Large-331M→Giant-1.3B, eight retrieval tasks
relationships.reason: M-L-MSR through M-L-FL and M-G-MSR through M-G-FL improve on every task at each size increase; this supports directional scale improvement only.
relationships.display_finding: All eight retrieval tasks improved at each model-size increase.

relationships.condition: Data-scale ablation, full nominal 1M→334M series on MSRVTT, VATEX, and AudioCaps
relationships.reason: D-1-MSR/D-334-MSR, D-1-VAT/D-334-VAT, and D-1-AC/D-334-AC show monotonic endpoint gains of 4.9, 3.1, and 5.1 Recall@1 points, respectively.
relationships.display_finding: Recall@1 increased monotonically, with endpoint gains of 4.9 points on MSRVTT, 3.1 on VATEX, and 5.1 on AudioCaps.

relationships.condition: Data-scale ablation, MSVD and ClothoV2 above nominal 10M
relationships.reason: D-110-MSVD/D-334-MSVD improve only 42.8→43.0→44.1, and D-110-CV2/D-334-CV2 only 15.9→17.1→17.5, showing modest gains despite much larger nominal datasets.
relationships.display_finding: Scores increased only 42.8→43.0→44.1 on MSVD and 15.9→17.1→17.5 on ClothoV2 despite much larger nominal datasets.

relationships.condition: Data-scale ablation, DIDEMO and COCO across nominal 10M→110M→334M
relationships.reason: D-110-DID and D-110-COCO decline 42.7→41.7 and 49.9→49.6 before recovering to 43.2 and 51.5; the relation is nonmonotonic, with no uncertainty reported.
relationships.display_finding: DIDEMO fell from 42.7 to 41.7 before recovering to 43.2, while COCO fell from 49.9 to 49.6 before reaching 51.5, without reported uncertainty.

relationships.reason: D-1-FL through D-334-FL give 77.5→77.1→78.1→80.9: eventual improvement includes a small initial reversal whose significance is unknown.
relationships.display_finding: Scores progressed 77.5→77.1→78.1→80.9, combining eventual improvement with an initial decline of unknown significance.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Model-scale ablation, Large-331M and Giant-1.3B across the eight reported retrieval metrics
reader_labels.reason: All reported scores rise over the Base-86M reference at the larger model sizes (rows M-L-MSR–M-L-FL and M-G-MSR–M-G-FL). This shows scale-associated improvement, not a fitted predictive law.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Data-scale ablation, especially DIDEMO(VA) and COCO(I) at 110M
reader_labels.reason: Scores generally end higher at 334M than at 10M, but DIDEMO(VA) and COCO(I) dip at 110M, so the observed data-scale relation is not uniformly monotonic (rows D-110-DID, D-110-COCO, D-334-DID, D-334-COCO).
